reviews.body: Needs to go through the clock so the date window is testable.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: Please use `clock.now()` from `app.utils.clock` here instead of `datetime.utcnow()`. Two reasons. Tests freeze time through the `frozen_clock` fixture, which only works if the code asks the clock; that's why your test has to compute `yesterday` from utcnow itself, and it will fail if CI runs it across midnight. And `utcnow()` returns a naive datetime while `captured_at` is timezone-aware, so the comparison in the repo query will blow up on postgres.

comments.author: dan
comments.body: Didn't know about the fixture. So the test should use `frozen_clock` and fixed dates instead?

comments.author: bob
comments.body: Yes. The fixture freezes to 2026-01-15 12:00, so put the factory objects on the 14th and the window is deterministic.

comments.author: dan
comments.body: Switched to `clock.now()` and rewrote the test with `frozen_clock`.

comments.author: frank

comments.author: alice
comments.body: Let's not spend review comments on import order. ruff and ruff-format run in pre-commit and fix this automatically. Dan, looks like the hook isn't installed on your machine: `pre-commit install` and it'll sort itself out on the next commit.
